messages:
alex: Proposal: split the 'residency' guarantee from 'prefetching' signals. We're currently overloading Lease/Pin for both and it's causing weird eviction and telemetry coupling.

alex: Concrete: two distinct APIs - Ownership (strong residency/lease semantics) and Prefetch (best-effort warm hints). Provide a compatibility shim for older clients during rollout.

jamie: +1. Quick correctness question: does Ownership still imply read liveness (i.e., read paths can skip remote fetch while token valid)?

alex: Yes. Ownership = local residency and read/write safety. Prefetch = anticipatory warm; no correctness or safety guarantees.

priya: Eviction policy concern: if prefetches are treated same as ownership, we'll keep churny warm-only keys in memory and lose QoS for real owners. We should make prefetch low-priority in eviction scoring.

sven: Exactly. Prefetches get a soft TTL and lower eviction weight. Ownership tokens are first-class inputs to eviction and handoff.

alex: Sketch of APIs:
```
// Ownership
claim_prefix(prefix_id) -> ownership_token
release_prefix(prefix_id, token)

// Prefetch
prefetch_prefix(prefix_id, priority=LOW, deadline_ms=1000)
```
Ownership token carries a residency_epoch and lease_id for handoff validation.

jamie: Handoff races are tricky. Current CAS-like dance caused subtle flakes in stress. How do we atomically move ownership?

sven: Use epoch + lease_id checks: receiver must ACK and swap resident lease_id in one atomic update. If epoch mismatch, abort and fallback. We still log and escalate as a safety path.

priya: Telemetry we need: tenant-scoped metrics: ownership_hit, ownership_miss, prefetch_requests, prefetch_wasted, eviction_reclaimed_bytes. Also histogramed read latency for ownership-hit vs miss. Ops will tune policies from that.

alex: Agree. Proposed metric names: kv.ownership.hits, kv.ownership.misses, kv.prefetch.requests, kv.prefetch.wasted, kv.eviction.reclaimed_bytes.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: creating canary group "kv-ownership-split-canary" in eng-runtime-alpha.

jamie: Migration plan: shim old API to call both new surfaces where appropriate. Feature-flag rollout: 0% -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% over days with rollback hooks. Clients accept legacy or new tokens.

alex: Data migration: persisted lease metadata gets new residency_epoch field and optional prefetch_meta blob. New servers read both; old ignores prefetch_meta.

sven: Safety: if epoch handshake fails during handoff, do conservative remote fetch instead of silent incorrect local hit. Emit an incident metric so we can triage.

priya: Testing: unit tests for claim/release races, simulated handoff collisions. Canary workload: hotkey generator that validates read success rates under heavy prefetch churn.

jamie: Ops playbook: if kv.prefetch.wasted spikes post-rollout, reduce prefetch rate or lower prefetch priority globally and inspect tenant policies.

alex: API ergonomics notes: keep OwnershipToken compact and cacheable locally (no RPC per read). Support batching prefetch calls: prefetch_prefix([p1,p2], priority).

priya: Security: tokens must be tenant-scoped and validated. Do not allow cross-tenant token reuse.

sven: Memory-pressure behavior: when node is >memory_threshold, drop soft prefetch entries preferentially via LRU-scoring.

alex: Action items: alex -> draft RFC + API definitions + migration plan (EOD Friday). jamie -> dashboard + histograms (Mon). priya -> stress tests + canary plan (next Wed). sven -> handoff state machine doc (Tue).

jamie: Add a read-only debug endpoint to enumerate active ownership tokens on a node (authz controlled) to aid incident triage.

alex: Will include that. Closing notes: will open PR to RFC repo, include example client shim and simple backward compatibility layer. Ping me if you want to pair on handoff tests.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: canary "kv-ownership-split-canary" started at 10% traffic; logs forwarded to /canary/kv-ownership-split.
